resolved_unknowns: scout unknown #1 RESOLVED, and it has TWO different answers depending on query style. drizzle-orm/postgres-js/driver.js:10-13 installs a transparentParser for OIDs 1082/1083/1114/1184, so postgres.js hands back the RAW Postgres text and never builds a Date.

(a) ORM path (db.select, used by apps/api/src/routes/regulations.ts:259-271, which is what feeds apps/web): drizzle pg-core/columns/timestamp.js mapFromDriverValue does new Date(value + plus-zero-offset) giving a UTC-midnight Date, then Fastify JSON.stringify emits 2026-09-01T00:00:00.000Z. apps/web NEVER receives a bare 2026-09-01.
(b) raw SQL path (db.execute, used by chat.ts, migration.ts, hunt.ts): the value stays the raw Postgres text 2026-09-01 00:00:00 with a space separator, no T and no Z.

Consequence, verified by running node with TZ=America/Chicago: new Date(2026-09-01) renders Aug 31 (bug). new Date(2026-09-01T00:00:00.000Z) renders Aug 31 (bug). new Date(2026-09-01 00:00:00) renders Sep 1 (V8 lenient non-ISO parse, treated as LOCAL, correct).

Therefore a split-on-dash parser with a trailing dollar anchor handles only the bare form and MISSES the ISO-Z form that apps/web actually receives. The parser must be un-anchored at the tail. See architect.fix_rule.

architect.lastScraped_verdict: EXCLUDED. states.lastScraped is timestamp(last_scraped) written by the scraper at scrape time - a real instant with a real time-of-day, not a date-only string. Rendering an instant in the reader local time is the semantically correct choice for a last-updated line. fix_rule.statement: ONE rule, specified here so three call sites cannot derive three different ones. For a value whose SEMANTICS are a calendar date (season start/end only): if the input is already a Date, return it UNTOUCHED - the caller has localized it (apps/mobile does exactly this) and shifting it again is the double-shift regression. If the input is a string, read the leading YYYY-MM-DD and construct a LOCAL-midnight Date from those three numbers.
fix_rule.reference_shape: const m = /^(d{4})-(d{2})-(d{2})/.exec(value); if (!m) return new Date(value); return new Date(Number(m[1]), Number(m[2]) - 1, Number(m[3]))
fix_rule.load_bearing_detail: The regex has NO trailing dollar anchor. That single missing character is what makes it match BOTH 2026-09-01 and 2026-09-01T00:00:00.000Z. apps/web only ever receives the second form, so an anchored regex fixes nothing there while looking correct in review. This is the concrete resolution of scout unknown #1.
fix_rule.why_local_midnight_not_utc_rendering: Normalizing to a local-midnight Date leaves formatDateRange existing getFullYear/getMonth/getDate comparisons and its toLocaleDateString calls correct as written. The alternative - keeping the UTC instant and passing timeZone UTC to toLocaleDateString - ALSO requires switching every comparison to getUTCFullYear/getUTCMonth/getUTCDate, and forgetting one silently breaks the same-month and same-year branches at month boundaries. Local-midnight is the smaller blast radius and makes the string path converge on what the Date path already does.
fix_rule.guardrail: Valid ONLY for date-only-semantics fields. Applying it to a true instant such as lastScraped would truncate the time-of-day and is forbidden by this plan.
